title: Case: Customer with a cracked planter asks where her replacement is
context: A large ceramic planter (order TG-2406, shipment DL-1937) arrived cracked on 2026-06-04. Whinmoor's Damage intake team runs the claim; Replacement authorisations decides replacements once intake is complete.
initial_request: I am writing by email because the portal is plainly a black hole. It is now six days since I reported a planter that arrived in two pieces, more or less. I sent photographs the same afternoon. Since then I have had: an automatic reply, a reminder that I have unread messages which turn out to be adverts, an email about replacing my pots which turned out to be an advert for more planters, and a refund of four pounds for some twine, which is not what I asked about. What I have not had is a single sentence from a human being about the planter. I have the broken one sitting in its box in my hallway taking up room. I sent you everything you could possibly need on day one. So where is my replacement, and when is someone coming for this one? If I do not hear by Friday I will be disputing the charge with my bank.

must: Asks Wystan Brackley for a photo of the outer box showing the shipping label
Gives the 2026-06-12 date by which Damage intake needs it for claim DC-8062
Makes clear the planter photos were received and that the replacement decision comes from Replacement authorisations after intake is complete
must_not: Tell her a replacement is approved, dispatched or on its way (the approved and collected replacement in the thread is DL-8288, another customer's trough)
Promise a replacement, refund, compensation or a collection date for the broken planter
Send the claim to Replacement authorisations before intake is complete
Ask her to resend the planter photos she has already supplied
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Dear Ms Brackley, I am sorry you have had no proper reply since the 4th. Your three photos of the planter were received and accepted, and damage claim DC-8062 is open for shipment DL-1937. One thing is still missing that nobody asked you for: a photo of the outer box showing the shipping label, so the carrier can match the carton. Whinmoor's Damage intake team needs it by 2026-06-12 or the claim closes automatically, so please keep the box and send that photo as soon as you can, by reply to this email. Once intake is complete, the decision on a replacement is made by Whinmoor's Replacement authorisations team; I cannot confirm that or a collection of the damaged planter for them, but I will pass your photo on the moment it arrives and tell you what they decide. Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk
